title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1970-02-27
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture with a crisp Charlie Miller transfer, highlighted by the NFA→Lovelight sequence and an inspired Easy Wind performance.
ai_review.review: The February 27 1970 Family Dog show shines thanks to stellar playing – Jerry’s guitar is in top form, the band rides a powerful NFA→Turn On Your Lovelight stretch and delivers an unforgettable Easy Wind.  The soundboard recording, expertly transferred by Charlie Miller, is clear and well‑balanced, making this a must‑have for collectors despite a few early‑year monitor quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (9 out of 13) give 4–5 stars and praise both the performance and the mix; only a few note minor flaws.  High‑quality soundboard source combined with standout songs yields an overall rating in the excellent range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix; Charlie Miller transfer praised as “impeccable”.  One reviewer notes early‑year monitor issues and a separate drum track that feels odd, but overall the audio is clean and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows naturally, building from a unique Cold Rain intro into the high‑energy NFA→Lovelight stretch, with acoustic interludes (Easy Wind) and strong vocal moments that keep momentum throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as playing his finest material; notable for a unique guitar intro on Cold Rain and tight lead work during Lovelight.
band_member_comments.Bob: His vocals on Me and My Uncle are highlighted as melodic; backing vocals with Weir and Pigpen receive special praise on Lovelight.
band_member_comments.Drums: One reviewer calls the separate “Drums” track absurd, but overall drumming is solid and contributes to the show’s energy.
